evidence: Method: built a criterion->requirement map for both gate criteria, all 41 functional criteria (tests/scored/functional/judge.toml lines 23-408), 5 polish binary criteria and 5 visual Likert criteria, plus every protocol step in the functional/polish/visual/gate prompts, against instruction.md (lines 1-17), environment/instructions/hireops_rules.md (sections 1-9) and integration.md. Verified each seed fact a criterion quotes against environment/assets/seed_data.json: Platform Engineer Applied = Greta Lindqvist(1), Ade Bello(2), Marco Rossi(3); Screen = Priya Nair(1), Samuel Ortiz(2) (hro_restart, protocol Z); APP-101 (Noor, Platform Engineer, Interview) note reads 'Strong systems answers; weaker on incident follow-up.'; APP-101 has 120 messages and thread_page_size is 30; Lena (USR-CAN3) has read_count 2 of 3 messages on APP-301 and the third is by USR-REC3, so 1 unread (protocol Z); candidate_status_labels match the hro_candidate_view wording; Ingrid (J1 manager) and Bill (J2 manager) are hiring_manager accounts. Requirement-backed (no false-fail found): 401 for anonymous callers (rules s1) in hro_anonymous; not-found for another application's conversation (rules s1 404) in hro_thread_access and hro_candidate_private; places 0/51/2.5 refused (s2 'a whole number from 1 to 50'); a non-hiring-manager as manager refused (s2); email refusal shown at the field with typed text kept (s2); one-stage moves, reject from any stage but Hired with a non-blank reason, reopen only to origin, reason cleared and restored by undo (s3 Moving a card, Undo); arrival at bottom and bulk board order A2,V and Y,W,X (s3 'by stage in the order listed above, then by place'); undo conflicts including another person's re-order of a moved card, with the unrelated-change control (s3 Undo 'moved, re-ordered, rejected or reopened since, by anyone'); undo once and earlier move no longer undoable (Z stays in Screen); a refused undo not consuming the undo (s3 'Undo is refused, changing nothing'); version-based stale refusal naming who (s3 Two people at once; instruction line 3); focus on the card's controls after refusal (s3 Shown at once); manager late-stage scope and refusals including re-ordering Applied and reopening a Screen rejection (s3 Who may move what); Activity coverage incl. re-orderings, each card of bulk moves, undos, newest first, per-job filter, Observer readable, no lines for refusals (s4); live board, unread and seen within 15 s and preservation of typing, focus, open card/conversation and scroll (instruction line 5; s5); Enter/Shift+Enter, emptied and focused box, failed send stays with notice (s6 Messages); latest 30 oldest-first scrolled to newest, 30 at a time with remaining count, anchor stays put (s6 Long conversations); per-person unread, total, scrolled-up notice (s6 Unread); seen rules incl. Observer never counts and the job's manager counts (s6 Seen); drafts per conversation/person/browser surviving view change, reload and session end, hidden from another user (s6 Drafts; instruction line 7); note drafts kept per person per browser (s3 Internal notes); candidate title/team/wording and the privacy field list incl. rejected-from stage and board place (s7); seeded data and restart persistence (instruction line 15; s9). Sign-in in the render gate is explicitly asked (instruction line 17) and in any case is house convention per the workbook Internal Quality Checks annotation on row 27 and the SKILL known false positive. Visual Likert rows grade desktop craft, which instruction line 11 asks for ('A clear desktop workspace is what matters'); visual prompt line 14 waives phone layout and themes. The hro_activity parenthetical '(notes and messages are not recorded in Activity ...)' adds no fail condition for apps that do record notes. Conditional display legs (source; team/manager/places 'wherever the app shows job details or are evidenced by behaviour') do not impose layout beyond the brief. Prompts say 'Do not require routes, selectors, field names, layouts or exact wording' (functional prompt line 15) and accept hidden controls with replay (line 23). Residual Notes, not demonstrated false-fails, reported because the row asks for every instance: (N1, P3) hro_stale_refused (functional/judge.toml line 200) with protocol C (functional/prompt.md line 33) performs the stale move only as a raw fetch replay, so its 'or on screen' leg cannot fire and the person must be identified in the HTTP refusal body (name, or an id the app's staff data resolves). The brief requires the person to be told who (instruction line 3; rules s3 'The person is told that the card was changed and by whom'), not that the API response carries it. A conforming app returning a bare 409 whose client then re-reads the board to display who moved the card would fail. The golden embeds the last Activity detail in its 409 message (solution/app/src/index.js:243-244), and the server naturally knows the actor, so this alternative is unlikely. (N2, P3) hro_reject_reason (line 83) requires staff to be able to read the rejected-from stage; rules s3 says only 'The workspace remembers the stage', but the criterion accepts the card, details, reopen control or Activity line, and an Activity line saying 'what changed' plus a reopen limited to that stage make it a reasonable professional default. (N3, P3) protocol B(12) treats Mei's re-order of Y as a change to another card that must not block undo of A2; Screen then reads Y,W,X,Z,A2, so any re-order of Y is downward and need not move A2, and rules s3 limit blocking to changes of 'those cards'. An app that bumps every Screen card's version on renumbering would fail, but that contradicts 'a version that changes whenever the card moves'. Runtime: raw-evidence-index.json (input_sha256 matches) lists only scripted golden observations and states that configured grading, Oracle and model scores are absent. Golden runs cannot measure a false-fail on a conforming alternative, so this verdict is a source-level judgement and claims no portal, Oracle or model result.
